messages.content: "你能告訴我著名足球運動員莱萊納爾·梅西的淨資產是多少歐元嗎？之後，我想知道籃球運動員勒布朗·詹姆斯的淨資產是多少英鎊。此外，我對一個使用公制系統的重85公斤、身高180公分的人的身體質量指數（BMI）也很好奇。最後，你能計算一個使用英制系統的重200磅、身高6英呎2英吋的人的BMI嗎？"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

message.reasoning:
The user asks for net worth of Messi in euros, net worth of LeBron James in pounds, BMI for metric person, BMI for imperial person. We have functions: celebrity_net_worth_get(name, currency) and calculate_bmi(weight, height, unit). For Messi: name "莱萊納爾·梅西" but likely "Lionel Messi". The function expects name string. Use "Lionel Messi". Currency: "EUR". For LeBron: name "LeBron James", currency "GBP". For BMI metric: weight 85 kg, height 180 cm, unit default metric. For BMI imperial: weight 200 lbs, height 6 ft 2 in. But calculate_bmi expects weight in kg and height in cm? It says weight in kilograms, height in centimeters. But unit optional to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric'. So we can pass weight 200, height 6*12+2=74 inches? But weight in kilograms? If unit imperial, weight should be in pounds? The function signature: weight: number, height: number, unit?: string. So if unit is 'imperial', weight is in pounds, height in inches. So we pass weight 200, height 74, unit 'imperial'. Good.

We need to call functions. We'll call celebrity_net_worth_get twice, calculate_bmi twice. Then combine results.
